scenarios: Cutover flips codec to rich; a comment with a heading/list is sent as json.dumps(ADF); ACLI posts the literal JSON string as the comment body

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the encode/fit/sanitize ordering for the Cloud comment path so length-fitting uses the rich ADF measure (fit_markdown_to_adf_limit) BEFORE serialization and the char guard never truncates the JSON-encoded body.
evidence: Repo: add_comment calls `body = _sanitize_comment(body)` (line 502) BEFORE building `--body` (line 511); _sanitize_comment truncates plaintext to _JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS (jira_fields.py:76-78)

Plan proposes `--body json.dumps(to_wire(body))` but is silent on the sanitize/fit ordering; AdfCodec.fit_outbound uses fit_markdown_to_adf_limit for the rich measure (rich_text_codec.py:52-53), implying fitting must precede serialization, not truncate the serialized JSON
findings.finding: The plan does not specify where the new ADF encode sits relative to `_sanitize_comment` (the 32,767-char guard at acli_cli_ops.py:502). If the encode happens before sanitize, the guard truncates a JSON-serialized ADF string — which both mismeasures the true body length and can slice the JSON mid-structure, producing an invalid ADF payload ACLI would reject.
scenarios: A near-limit comment is rendered to ADF (JSON expands well past 32,767 chars), the existing plaintext guard truncates the JSON string, and ACLI receives malformed JSON

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify an expand-contract backfill for the dedup-key migration: before/at codec flip, populate the `local_comment_key -> Jira comment ID` map (or a dual-key read window comparing both the identity-normalized and codec-rendered keys) for comments already mirrored under the old body-equality regime, so the flip cannot re-post legacy comments that carry neither a map entry nor a `jira_comment_id`.
evidence: Plan: 'Flipping the comment path to the real codec, and keeping comment-diff convergent when it renders rich, is this story's job.'
Plan section 1b DEMOTES the body-equality test only 'against a lost map write' -- it does not cover legacy comments that never had a map entry.

The map is populated only forward: '1a. Capture the returned ID at both enactment sites' (outbound create) and inbound-origin `jira_comment_id`; no step backfills the map for comments mirrored before the story.

3388 comment audit: after such a codec shift 'every already-mirrored comment's key would shift to its rendered form while Jira still holds plain text, so every comment would read as absent and the differ would re-post the project's entire comment history'.
findings.finding: The dedup-key migration (flipping `_resolve_codec` from `_IdentityCodec` to the real `RichTextCodec`) changes how the local comment identity key is computed for EVERY comment, but the plan provides no backfill/expand path for comments already mirrored before this story's map existed. Such legacy comments have no map entry and (unless inbound-origin) no `jira_comment_id`, so at the moment the codec flips their only guard is the DEMOTED body-equality skip -- which now computes the local key with the real codec (rendered wire) while Jira still holds the pre-cutover wire, matching exactly the 're-post the entire comment history' hazard the 3388 audit flagged. The migration is not expand-contract: nothing pre-populates the map for pre-existing comments before the codec flip.
findings.location: Approach section 2 ('flip the a32a codec injection ... from `_IdentityCodec` to the real `RichTextCodec`') and section 1b ('the normalized-body test ... is DEMOTED ... to a secondary skip against a lost map write')
scenarios: An operator flips the cutover flag on a project with an existing mirrored comment history; on the next pass the rendered local keys no longer match the plain-text Jira wire and no map entry exists, so the differ re-posts every historical comment.
A DC binding whose comments were mirrored under the identity normalizer is migrated: convergence is only tested for the post-map world, not for the legacy no-map-entry population.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a backfill step (or a transitional dual-key skip) covering pre-existing comments: on the first post-cutover pass, treat a legacy comment as already-synced when EITHER the rendered key OR the identity-normalized key matches a Jira comment, and record the discovered Jira ID into the map at that point. Add an AC/test for the legacy population (no map entry, no jira_comment_id) proving zero re-post across the flip, distinct from the already-covered crash-durability and post-map convergence cases.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State and test the post-rollback comment-identity invariant: with the ID map as the codec-independent PRIMARY guard, flipping the cutover flag back OFF must not re-post or re-diverge already-mapped comments; add an AC covering a rollback pass over a map populated during the rendered-codec window.
evidence: Plan depends on 3388 whose cutover flag is per-client and reversible ('off = plain/identity wire (the rollback)').

Plan's ID-map guard is PRIMARY and codec-independent, which likely holds across a rollback, but the plan never states this invariant nor tests it -- the back-out state of comment identity is unasserted.
T11 POST-ROLLBACK guidance: a back-out can 'report success while leaving persisted state incorrectly interpreted'.
findings.finding: The plan asserts convergence and crash-durability but never states the post-rollback / mixed-fleet interpretation of the map + codec flip. Because the cutover flag is per-client (inherited from 3388: enable Cloud then DC after canary) and the codec flip is what shifts the key, a rollback (flag back OFF) reverts the local key from rendered to identity form while the map now holds IDs recorded under the rendered regime. The plan does not assert what happens to comment identity after such a back-out (whether the map entries remain authoritative and prevent re-post, or whether the reverted identity key re-diverges).
findings.location: Approach section 2 (codec flip) and section 1b (two identity stores); Acceptance Criteria (no rollback-state AC)
scenarios: Operator canaries the cutover on one client, then rolls the flag back to OFF; the local dedup key reverts to identity form but the map holds IDs recorded during the rendered window.
A mixed pass where some comments were mapped under rendered keys and the codec is now identity again.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit invariant that the map's `local_comment_key -> Jira ID` skip is evaluated BEFORE any codec-dependent body key, so identity survives a codec flip in either direction, and pin it with a rollback test (flag on -> record IDs -> flag off -> assert zero new comments).
